issue.body:
To access a related model in twig, e.g. a model's "owner", you can use `{{ model.owner }}`. However, when model's owner is NULL, you get an exception: `Object of class yii\db\ActiveQuery could not be converted to string`

Apparently, when resolving a variable, Twig uses isset() to determine if the variable can be retrieved via the object's ArrayAccess. If the relation is not null this all goes according to plan, but if it _is_ null, it falls back to using call_user_func on the object and ends up fetching the ActiveQuery object that's returned by getOwner().

I do think it's somewhat confusing in Yii2's architecture that you define a function getRelation() that returns an ActiveQuery, but calling $model->relation gets you the resolved relation instead of an ActiveQuery. Wouldn't it be less ambiguous if relations were defined like 'public function getOwnerRelation' or 'public function relationOwner'?

In general I would be even happier with a different solution for view inheritance though. Using twig adds a lot of extra quirks and overhead, while the only reason I need it is the template inheritance. Ideas?
